terms.gloss: say or do a second time, repeat
evidence: Cic. Att. 14.14.1: Iterādum eadem ista mihi.
terms.comment: From iterum, “a second time”: to say the same words again, or do a thing again (pugnam iterāre, Liv. 6.32). In farming it is to plough a second time (Lewis & Short).

evidence: Traupman 34: repete quid modo dīxerīs, repeat what you just said
Traupman 34: repeat the passage, repete (repetite) locum
terms.comment: To go back over what was said or begun, so also to resume; Traupman’s classroom word. Its first senses are to attack again and to go back for, fetch, or claim back (rēs repetere); Lewis & Short.
The plain way: Dīc iterum, say it again. Traupman 34 has eīsdem verbīs mihi redde for “repeat after me”.

terms.grammar: reddō with the ablative eīsdem verbīs
evidence: Cic. Brut. 301: ut quae sēcum commentātus esset, ea sine scrīptō verbīs eīsdem redderet (Lewis & Short s.v. reddō)
Traupman 34: repeat after me, eīsdem verbīs mihi redde (reddite)
terms.comment: Reddere is to give back what one has heard or learned, so “repeat after me” is eīsdem verbīs mihi redde, “give it back to me in the same words”.

sources: Lewis & Short: itero · Lewis & Short: repeto
Cic. Att. 14.14.1 checked against the Perseus Latin texts (Purser, who prints Iteradum as one word; 11 November 2026).

Lewis & Short: reddo
Quotations marked “Lewis & Short” are given as Lewis & Short cites them, in the house spelling; they have not been checked against a modern edition.
